row.title: Gaussian density integrals for supplied length measures
row.statement:
For $d\in\{1,2\}$, suppose a countably additive measure $\lambda_d$ on $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d)$ is supplied and satisfies
$$\lambda_d\!\left(\prod_{j=1}^d(a_j,b_j]\right)=\prod_{j=1}^d(b_j-a_j)\qquad(a_j<b_j).$$
No assertion about constructing these measures is made.

1. If $Q$ is a nondegenerate compact box and $h:Q\to\mathbb R$ is bounded, Borel measurable and Riemann integrable, then its integral against the supplied measure equals its proper Riemann integral. Nonnegative Borel functions on the whole space are computed from increasing compact-box cutoffs by monotone convergence.
2. For the supplied $\lambda_1$, every $m\in\mathbb R$, $v>0$ and
$$g_{m,v}(x)=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi v}}e^{-(x-m)^2/(2v)}$$
satisfy
$$\int g_{m,v}\,d\lambda_1=1,\qquad \int xg_{m,v}(x)\,d\lambda_1(x)=m,\qquad \int(x-m)^2g_{m,v}(x)\,d\lambda_1(x)=v.$$
The signed first moment is absolutely integrable. These are density-integral statements and require no choice axiom in addition to the supplied measures.
row.axiom_use: None beyond the explicitly supplied countably additive Borel measures with their box-volume contract. The proof does not construct Lebesgue measure or a normal probability law.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, Chapter 4; local Darboux comparison and Gaussian calculation under supplied measures

row.title: An optimized mean-field law can lose posterior correlation
row.statement: Optimizing an independent Gaussian mean-field family by the evidence lower bound need not recover the marginal variances or dependence structure of the exact inferential target.

references.title: David M. Blei, Alp Kucukelbir, and Jon D. McAuliffe, Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians, §2.3 and Figure 1
Michael I. Jordan et al., An Introduction to Variational Methods for Graphical Models, §6.3.1
Ronghuo Zheng, Zhiting Hu, and Yuntian Deng, 10-708 Probabilistic Graphical Models, Lecture 13: Variational Inference II, complete 9-page lecture note

row.axiom_use: None beyond the reference length and area measures supplied in the example. Their Borel restrictions satisfy the box-volume contract; finite Darboux bounds, explicit cutoffs, and compact Gaussian integration prove all normalizers and moments without constructing Lebesgue measure or using AC-dependent normal laws.

row.title: Positive ABC tolerance changes an identity-summary target
row.statement: With the identity summary and positive prior-predictive acceptance probability, the tolerance $\epsilon=3/5$ gives an ABC target whose mass at $\theta=1$ is $9/17$, while the exact posterior mass is $4/5$; the total-variation distance is exactly $23/85$.

references.title: Jarno Lintusaari et al., Fundamentals and Recent Developments in Approximate Bayesian Computation, PDF pp. 1-6, 10-23, 46-47
Paul Fearnhead and Dennis Prangle, Constructing Summary Statistics for Approximate Bayesian Computation: Semi-automatic ABC, PDF pp. 1-18, 35-38

row.axiom_use: None. All probabilities and tolerance-ball events are finite and explicit; the rejection statement assumes an IID proposal-simulator sequence as stated in its supplier.
